reason: The passage names two characters: Moses and Pharaoh. While Pharaoh is clearly established as a leader (king of Egypt), Moses is not portrayed as a leader in this passage. When Moses intervenes in a dispute between Hebrew men, one explicitly rejects his authority with a sarcastic challenge: 'Who made you a ruler and judge over us?' (לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ). Moses is presented here as a fugitive without leadership status or authority, having fled Egypt after killing an Egyptian man. He has not yet been called to his prophetic role.
